findings.evidence: Lines 202–210 define the equivalence and its application formula using only Mathlib objects and injectivity of mixedEmbedding, without any reduced-basis dependency.
findings.fix: Relocate and export integerLatticeEquiv and coe_integerLatticeEquiv in canonical-embedding infrastructure; annotate the application lemma with @[simp].
findings.issue: The canonical equivalence between integers and their embedded lattice is private, preventing reuse independently of reduced bases.

findings.evidence: The definition at lines 279–281 is a finite supremum; house_reducedIntegralBasis_le supplies only one direction, and integralBasisHouse_le itself unfolds the definition at line 319.
findings.fix: Add integralBasisHouse_def and an @[simp] characterization integralBasisHouse K ≤ c ↔ ∀ i, house (reducedIntegralBasis K i : K) ≤ c.
findings.issue: integralBasisHouse lacks a characteristic upper-bound API: consumers cannot prove a bound from bounds on every basis member without unfolding its hidden finite supremum.

summary: The reduced-basis API hides reusable infrastructure and does not fully characterize its maximum-house constant.
